DECISIONS:
Q1: DERIVE_FROM_REPO
Q2: A
Q3: A
Q4: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: Option A needs #9130's approved file list and its Q3/Q4 option text pasted in. Neither is in the repository: no file mentions 9130. #9130 is closed and its PR #9134 sits on a branch that is not checked out, so the data-provision guard rules out A. This decision takes option B's approach: this issue's five numbered items plus this record's Q2–Q4 answers are the whole spec. This issue's own "Q3: A and Q4: A" maps onto Q3:A and Q4:A here. The file list below is taken from the repository so the planner does not have to guess it.
Q2: The repository already has a tested way to re-run failed jobs. `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py` `rerun_failed_jobs` (lines 294-304) makes one `POST .../actions/runs/{run_id}/rerun-failed-jobs`, requires `HTTP/... 201`, never prints the response body, and never falls back to a full re-run. Option A matches that, while B and C would compete with it (§9). There is no "transient" field in triage diagnosis today (`scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` and the triage scripts have no such classifier). So "transient" is defined from the existing deterministic classifier `classify_runner_shutdown` (line 356), not from free-text model output.
Q3: Keeping today's triage issue post unchanged preserves existing behaviour (§2.1). Only one POST is added. The `open_head_rerun` path in Q4 then closes the issue on its own once the re-run passes. Option B would conflict with Q4:A, as the question's own note says.
Q4: `_verify_open_head` (`scripts/check_triage_resolution.py:675-747`) currently fails at line 694-695 with `open_head_unchanged` whenever the head has not moved. That is exactly the case a same-head re-run produces. Option A adds a resolution path for that case and leaves the `open_head` and `merged` paths and every existing reason code unchanged.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml (stage steps use `CHECK_TRIAGE_STAGE`; GH_PAT stage env at lines 625-627, 672-674; feature-flag env defaults at lines 248-256)
    - scripts/check_failure_triage.sh (stage dispatch `TRIAGE_STAGE="${CHECK_TRIAGE_STAGE:-all}"` line 440; stage list documented at line 49)
    - scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py (`rerun_failed_jobs` line 294, `classify_runner_shutdown` line 356)
    - scripts/check_triage_resolution.py (`_verify_open_head` line 675)
    - scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py (`_plan_grant_path` line 835, `_PLAN_GRANT_BARE_FILE_RE` line 827, `_PLAN_GRANT_FILE_SEGMENT_RE` line 832)
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml line 2459 (`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_check_failure_triage_post_stage.py`)
    - tests/test_check_triage_resolution.py, tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py, tests/test_check_failure_triage_post_stage.py, tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py
  steps:
    - The plan may change only these files: `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml`, `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`, `scripts/check_triage_resolution.py`, `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py`, the new `tests/test_check_failure_triage_transient_rerun.py`, `tests/test_check_triage_resolution.py`, `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, one `changelog.d/` fragment and one `agents.d/<issue>-<slug>.md` fragment.
    - `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py` is read-only. Import `rerun_failed_jobs` and `classify_runner_shutdown` from it; do not copy their logic. If the import is impossible, add the new script to the list and record why.
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_check_failure_triage_transient_rerun.py` to the same `run:` block as line 2459. Do not edit `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`.
    - `_plan_grant_path`: keep the existing `_headers`/`_redirects` handling at line 851 as is. An extensionless last segment that fails `_PLAN_GRANT_FILE_SEGMENT_RE` is granted only if the path is a regular file in the planning checkout. Never grant a directory. A missing path holds the plan as replannable, without silently dropping it. Do not cut lines from the existing guard or its tests beyond what this change needs. This is the regression the issue's "Why" section names.
    - Each new identifier (`open_head_rerun`, `CHECK_TRIAGE_TRANSIENT_RERUN_ENABLED`, the stage name) must be checked to be unique. Rename or remove nothing; confirm with `git diff isolated-base`.
    - Checks to run: the tests named above, plus `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` and `tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py`, all with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. Also run `bash -n scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` and `wc -c` on each changed workflow (must be under 480000 bytes).
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "#9130's approved plan file list and its Q3:A / Q4:A text"
  equivalence_argument: The five numbered items in this issue already name every behaviour #9130's Q3/Q4 covered: the re-run stage, `open_head_rerun` and the grant fix. This record's Q2–Q4 decide them with code anchored to existing repo files. The file list covers each of those behaviours and nothing else, so scope cannot quietly grow or shrink.
  reversibility: If a human later supplies #9130's original Q3/Q4 text and it differs, only the Q2–Q4 behaviour changes. Each part is behind `CHECK_TRIAGE_TRANSIENT_RERUN_ENABLED` or a single new path name, and nothing existing is renamed, so reverting is a plain revert.
Q2:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py `rerun_failed_jobs` (one POST, 201 check, body never printed) and `classify_runner_shutdown` (returns shutdown / action_resolution / checkout_fetch / abandoned / genuine / unverified)
  steps:
    - Add a `transient-rerun` stage to `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`, run from its own step in `check_failure_triage.yml` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}`. Never use `CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN`. Add env `CHECK_TRIAGE_TRANSIENT_RERUN_ENABLED: ${{ vars.CHECK_TRIAGE_TRANSIENT_RERUN_ENABLED || 'true' }}`, and give the script a default of `true` too (§8).
    - The failure counts as transient only when `classify_runner_shutdown` returns `shutdown`, `action_resolution`, `checkout_fetch` or `abandoned`. `genuine`, `unverified` or any exception means no POST.
    - Skip without a POST in any of these cases: the flag is not `true`; there is no workflow run (only a check run, no run id); this is a historical triage (`CHECK_TRIAGE_HISTORICAL_RUN_ID` is set); the triaged run's `run_attempt` is greater than 1. That last rule caps re-runs at one per run, matching the attempt-1 scope of `classify_runner_shutdown`.
    - Make exactly one POST through `rerun_failed_jobs`, with no retry. Log the outcome as one line that carries no secrets. Any error, timeout or non-201 response is logged and the stage exits 0 (fail open), so the triage issue post is never blocked.
    - Tests in `tests/test_check_failure_triage_transient_rerun.py`: flag off means no POST; each non-transient verdict means no POST; run_attempt above 1 means no POST; a 201 response is logged as success; a non-201 response or an exception exits 0; GH_PAT is wired to this step only.
  equivalence_argument: Re-running only the failed jobs, and only after the repo's deterministic transient classification, is the narrowest form of option A. It reuses the code that already does this safely for the review sweep.
  reversibility: Setting the repository variable `CHECK_TRIAGE_TRANSIENT_RERUN_ENABLED=false` turns the stage into a no-op.
Q4:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/check_triage_resolution.py lines 694-747 (existing workflow-run and check-run checks on the current head)
  steps:
    - When `current == triage_head`, use the same checks as the existing `open_head` branch, applied to that same SHA. With `workflow_id` set: the latest pull_request run for the SHA must be completed and successful, have `run_attempt` greater than 1, and satisfy `shard_jobs_resolved` for `verdict["failed_jobs"]`. Without `workflow_id`: the latest check run for `check_name` on the SHA must be classified `success`.
    - On success, set `status="resolved"`, `reason="verified"`, `path="open_head_rerun"`, `evidence_sha=current`, `triage_head_sha=triage_head`. In every other case return `open_head_unchanged` exactly as today.
    - Add tests to `tests/test_check_triage_resolution.py`: a successful re-run resolves via `open_head_rerun`; no re-run, or a pending or failed one, still gives `open_head_unchanged`; the existing `open_head` and `merged` tests are unchanged.
  equivalence_argument: This is the same evidence standard the existing `open_head` path uses, applied to a re-run on the unchanged head, so no weaker proof can close an issue.
  reversibility: The new path only ever replaces an `open_head_unchanged` result. Removing it restores today's behaviour exactly.

SETUP REQUIRED (only when a decision relies on a placeholder):
- None. `GH_PAT` is already a declared secret in `check_failure_triage.yml` (line 55).
